hook.text: Vacuum-sealed steak lasts 3–5 weeks in the fridge versus 3–5 days unwrapped. Removing air is the simplest way to multiply shelf.

buildup.text: Vacuum packaging removes 99% of air from the package, then heat-seals it. Without oxygen, aerobic bacteria can't grow and fats.

discovery.text: Sous vide cooking depends on vacuum packaging—food is sealed, then cooked in precise water baths.

twist.text: Vacuum conditions allow anaerobic bacteria (like C. botulinum) to grow. Refrigeration remains essential.

climax.text: Dry-aged beef is exposed to air on purpose—controlled decomposition develops intense flavor.

punchline.text: Remove air, slow spoilage. But don't skip refrigeration.

quiz.question: Why must vacuum-packed meat still be refrigerated?
options: Anaerobic bacteria like C. botulinum can still grow without oxygen
